This beta continues the DSL 3.0 and Kubernetes stabilization work from beta.2.
It includes cloud execution, recovery, migration, and packaging fixes while
retaining beta status: the complete mixed Linux/Windows and real agentic
acceptance procedure remains outstanding.

## Highlights

- Harden remote authentication, OIDC trust, worker identity, and literal stage
  data handling across the Kubernetes dispatch boundary.
- Deliver cancellation to running stage pods and wait for bounded cleanup;
  handle resident sidecars and preserve retry identity, placement, and artifacts.
- Reconstruct admission budgets correctly after restart, including paired
  scheduler and engine start records for the same run.
- Preserve prepared artifacts, declared repository handoffs, harness selection,
  and scoped credentials across fresh stage attempts.
- Reject ambiguous YAML migrations and align DSL validation, placement, and
  release support metadata.
- Add instance-root identity and historical-root mutation guards, expose
  per-PR queue eligibility, and distinguish reviewer deferral from rejection
  and mechanical escalation.
- Verify final signed archives and native container images before publication,
  including quickstart, demo, portal, checksum, and prerelease installer checks.

## Known limitations

- DSL 3.0 remains preview and requires explicit opt-in. DSL 2.0 remains the
  supported compatibility contract; this beta does not establish a DSL 3.0 GA lock.
- DSL 1.4 is unsupported in the 0.4 release line. The support matrix records
  the actual early removal with `effectiveIn: v0.4.0` while preserving the
  previously promised v0.5.0 history. Use `goobers fix --to 2.0` to migrate.
- Local Linux tests have demonstrated cancellation, restart budgets, network
  isolation, repository publication, and builtin/local-ci recovery. They do
  not establish the full single-procedure S1–S9 acceptance or real agentic
  pod/node recovery. See `docs/releases/v0.4.0-rc.1-readiness.md` for scoped evidence.
- Official container-image publication and the corresponding distributed
  acceptance remain tracked by #3275. Native image build checks alone do not
  publish a supported image set.
- The reference control plane uses a single writer and RWO journal storage;
  replacement requires a bounded outage. Windows service startup checks
  establish bounded process liveness, not authenticated application readiness.
- The automatic installer intentionally accepts stable releases only. To test
  beta.3, download its platform archive and verify it against `SHA256SUMS`.
